newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: HOWARD REJECTS FOREIGN TRADE ZONE FOR NEWCASTLE
The Prime Minister has ruled out a special foreign trade zone for BHP's proposed Steel River project in Newcastle.
John Howard says such a scheme would have to be available across Australia for constitutional reasons.
A foreign trade zone would allow a company tax breaks to help it establish a local presence.
However the Prime Minister has announced a $500,000 program to rehabilitate Lake Macquarie, $1-million to boost tourism and $850,000 to go towards a waste recycling plant in the Hunter.
COAL COMPANY MORE CONFIDENT ABOUT RESOLVING DISPUTE
Rio Tinto says there may be light at the end of the tunnel in its five-week old dispute with the miners union at its Hunter valley Number One colliery, in New South Wales.
The Miners' Union says it wants to negotiate with Rio Tinto on an enterprise agreement while individual contracts remain on offer to union members, and while workers remain on strike.
Mine manager, Allan Davies, says the offer is an unusual one but the company is prepared to consider it.
Mr Davies says last week the union said it wasn't interested in taking Australian Workplace Agreements off the table, and today he has heard that is the cause.
"I wouldn't say it's a backdown. I think commonsense has to prevail sooner or later, and what I'm prepared to do is to give some consideration to a negotiation," he said.
HERRON ANNOUNCES HERITAGE PROTECTION REVIEW
Federal Aboriginal Affairs Minister John Herron has announced details of plans to review the Heritage Protection Act.
Speaking in Darwin today, Senator Herron announced a Commonwealth proposal to ask the States and Territories to develop their own legislation meeting minimum standards.
The Heritage Protection Act is the piece of law at the centre of the dispute over Hindmarsh Island in South Australia.
Senator Herron also announced wide-ranging terms of reference for a review of the Northern Territory Land Rights Act, with a report expected early next year.
ALL CLEAR GIVEN AFTER MELBOURNE EXPLOSION
Police have declared safe a street in the Melbourne suburb of Flemington, following an explosion in a back yard garage.
Houses in Mooltan Street were rocked by the blast, windows were blown out and roof tiles dislodged.
The arson squad and forensic experts have arrived to examine the badly damaged garage and adjoining properties.
There've been no injuries although a resident three doors down, Laura Gamvros, says she was terrified.
The policeman in charge of the scene, Det Sgt Martin Alison, says the explosive appears to be a commercially available device not a home made concoction.
BORBIDGE WILL BACK LABOR REPLACEMENT FOR COLSTON
Queensland Premier Rob Borbidge says he will now support a Labor nominee to fill the Senate vacancy if Independent Senator Mal Colston is forced to resign.
Senator Colston is facing charges of defrauding the Government over his parliamentary travel entitlements.
Mr Borbidge has backed away from an earlier threat to replace Senator Colston with an Independent if he's forced to go.
However, Mr Borbidge stopped short of supporting calls for the Senator to stand down.
He says everyone is innocent in Australia until proven guilty.
Mr Borbidge says if the charges were against a minister he would be expected to stand aside.
But he says in the case of a backbench MP or a Senator, who doesn't hold executive responsibility in Government, it's only reasonable that the law take its course.
RANSOM DEMAND REDUCED COURT TOLD
A Sydney Court has been told that two men allegedly reduced a ransom demand by $150,000 after kidnapping a woman at gun-point yesterday.
Bail was today refused for Thai Minh Lee and Johnnie Yeap, who appeared in Fairfield Local Court in Sydney's south-west to face armed robbery, kidnapping and extortion offences.
The men allegedly abducted a 23-year old woman as she returned home from the Sydney Casino with her de facto husband and with $3,000 in cash and $35,000 in casino chips.
It's alleged the men held the woman for 15 hours and threatened to harm her unborn child unless a ransom ranging from $200,000 to $50,000 was paid.
The woman was released uninjured last night after police converged on a ransom pick-up point in Fairfield.
